metaDescription: Seven AprilAire whole-house humidifiers compared on gallons per day, coverage, bypass vs fan-powered vs steam designs and HVAC installation needs.
expertTake: The AprilAire 700 is the pick for most forced-air homes, with 18 gallons per day, a built-in fan and automatic control. The 720AKZ is the newer, water-saving upgrade for larger houses. The 400 is the water saver for modest homes, the 300 suits boilers and ductless heat, and the 800 steam unit is for very large houses. All of these are installed into the HVAC system and should be fitted by a licensed HVAC professional. Skip a whole-house unit for a single dry room.
introParagraphs: A whole-house humidifier is installed into the heating system rather than set on a table, and it adds moisture to the air that the furnace distributes through the home. It is the right tool for a dry house through the heating season, because a portable unit cannot keep up with a whole building's air changes. The buying problem is that the model families work differently and the coverage numbers assume a tight house.

This guide explains how bypass, fan-powered and steam designs differ, how to read capacity against your home's real leakiness, and what the installation involves. Because these units connect to ducts, plumbing and wiring, a licensed HVAC professional should install them. Start with the picks above, then read the reviews below to match a model to your heating system and your house.

products.name: AprilAire 700 Automatic Fan-Powered Whole-House Humidifier

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Up to 5,300 sq ft in tightly built homes

specList.label: Mounting
specList.value: Warm-air plenum on forced-air furnace or heat pump

products.description:
The 700 is the model most homeowners should price first, because it removes the one limit that holds back the bypass models: it carries its own fan. A bypass humidifier relies on the pressure difference between the supply and return ducts to push air through the water panel, which varies from house to house. The 700 pulls heated air directly from the furnace with a built-in fan, so output no longer depends on duct pressure. AprilAire rates it at 18 gallons per day and up to 5,300 square feet in a tightly built home.

The automatic version adds dual sensors, one for indoor humidity and one for outdoor temperature, so the setpoint drops as the weather gets colder to avoid window condensation. Compared with the 600 at 17 gallons, it adds only about a gallon of rated capacity but delivers it more consistently. Compared with the 720AKZ at 21 gallons per day, it is the older, simpler design with a higher water use.

The unit mounts on the warm-air supply plenum, needs a water line and a drain, and needs a 120 volt connection for the fan, which is why a licensed HVAC professional should install it. Ownership is a water panel change once a year before the heating season, and cleaning mineral scale from the distribution tray. Hard water shortens panel life, and the panel is the part most owners forget.
products.bestFor: Homes of 3,000 to 5,000 square feet with a forced-air furnace and a desire for set-and-forget control.

Automatic mode adjusts for outdoor temperature
Eighteen gallons per day covers larger tightly built homes

cons: Needs a 120 V connection, adding to installation work

Needs a licensed installer for water, drain and wiring

products.name: AprilAire 720AKZ Fan-Powered Whole-House Humidifier

specList.label: Level tolerance
specList.value: Up to 3 degrees out of level

products.description:
The 720AKZ is the redesigned fan-powered humidifier and the one to look at if your house is large or your water is hard. It delivers 21 gallons per day, the highest evaporative rating in this lineup, and covers up to 6,250 square feet in a tightly built home. A recirculation valve reuses water, and AprilAire says that cuts wastewater by 60 percent compared with the 700. A hybrid fan spreads air across the panel for what the maker calls twice the evaporative efficiency on high speed.

It also fixes the chores. The one-piece HydroCore cartridge pops in and out for the annual change, the fan module can be reversed to fit tight installs including horizontal furnaces, and the distribution tray tolerates up to 3 degrees out of level. A catch-all drain reduces leak risk. Compared with the 700, the capacity is about 17 percent higher. Compared with the 800 steam unit, it is evaporative and uses far less electricity.

The automatic digital control adjusts humidity by outdoor temperature, and the 5 year warranty is the best in this roundup. It is part of AprilAire's Healthy Air System, which includes ventilation and filtration. Installation still needs water, drain, plenum cutting and 120 volt wiring, so use an HVAC professional. This listing is the automatic AKZ version.
products.bestFor: Larger homes and hard-water areas where the newer water-saving design and easier panel changes pay off.

Recirculation valve cuts wastewater by 60 percent vs the 700
One-piece HydroCore panel makes annual changes simple

Newer design has a shorter field record than the 700

products.name: AprilAire 600 Automatic High-Output Bypass Humidifier

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Up to 5,000 sq ft in tightly built homes

specList.label: Display
specList.value: Humidity, panel change and service lights

specList.label: Blower option
specList.value: Run continually or with the furnace

products.description:
The 600 is the high-output bypass model, and it is the practical choice when the furnace and ducting suit a bypass layout. It uses the furnace blower, with no fan of its own, to push air through the water panel via a bypass duct between supply and return. That means no electrical connection beyond the low-voltage control wiring, which simplifies the install compared with the fan-powered units. AprilAire rates it at 17 gallons per day and up to 5,000 square feet.

The tradeoff is that output depends on the furnace running and on the duct pressure difference. On a mild day the furnace runs less, so the humidifier runs less, which is why the 600 has a blower activation switch that can run the blower continuously. Compared with the 700, it has about the same rated capacity but depends on the furnace. Compared with the 400, which rates the same 17 gallons per day, it drains water continuously instead of evaporating all of it, giving higher output and a more tolerant of hard water.

The digital control shows humidity, lights for panel change and service, and the automatic mode adjusts to outdoor temperature. Annual maintenance is a water panel swap and a check of the drain. Installation needs a cut-in on the plenum and ducts, a water line and a drain, so use a professional.
products.bestFor: Homes with a suitable bypass duct layout that want high output without a 120 V fan.

products.name: AprilAire 400 Automatic Water Saver Humidifier

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Up to 5,000 sq ft in tightly built homes

specList.label: Water use
specList.value: Evaporates 100% of water to the panel

products.description:
The 400 is the water-saving bypass model, and the reason to choose it is that it does not send water down the drain. Instead of flushing the water panel continuously, it evaporates all the water that flows into it, per AprilAire. That also removes the need for a drain line in many installs, which can be a big advantage when the furnace is far from a floor drain. The rating is 17 gallons per day for up to 5,000 square feet in a tightly built home.

The tradeoff is minerals. All the dissolved solids from the water stay on the panel and the distribution parts, so hard water scales the panel faster than on a draining unit. Compared with the 600, which also rates 17 gallons, it saves water but will need more frequent panel changes and cleaning in hard water areas. Compared with the 700, it depends on the furnace blower.

The automatic control adjusts to outdoor temperature. Installation is a bypass duct, a water line and low-voltage wiring, and the water line should be done by someone who knows how to avoid leaks over a furnace. If your water hardness is high, or if you want to avoid a drain, have an HVAC pro confirm the match before purchase.
products.bestFor: Homes where a drain line is hard to run and the water is moderately soft.

products.name: AprilAire 300 Self-Contained Fan-Powered Humidifier

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Up to 3,900 sq ft in tightly built homes

specList.label: Compatible with
specList.value: Forced air, boilers, mini-splits, radiant heat

products.description:
The 300 is the one for houses that cannot use a furnace-mounted humidifier. It is self-contained with its own fan, so it does not depend on a furnace blower, which makes it usable with boilers, mini-splits, radiant heat and other ductless systems as well as ducted forced-air systems. AprilAire rates it at 13 gallons per day and up to 3,900 square feet in a tightly built home.

It needs a different mindset. Without a duct system to carry the moisture, you place the unit in a central area or tie it into a ducted system, and the output spreads by the home's own air movement. Compared with the 700, it holds 5 fewer gallons per day and has a manual rather than automatic control. Compared with the 500M, it nearly matches the capacity and adds that independence from the furnace.

The digital humidistat has an onboard sensor and you set the target by hand, so you need to lower it as the weather turns cold. It still needs a water supply, a drain or a defined water path, and a power connection. Because it can be placed in unusual locations, a professional should plan the water and drain runs. It suits an older home with radiant heat or a new build with mini-splits.
products.bestFor: Homes with boilers, radiant heat or mini-splits where no furnace plenum exists.

products.name: AprilAire 500M Manual Compact Furnace Humidifier

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Up to 3,600 sq ft in tightly built homes

products.description:
The 500M is the compact, manual bypass humidifier for smaller homes. It rates at 12 gallons per day and up to 3,600 square feet in a tightly built home. It has a single sensor in the standard control that monitors indoor humidity, and you set the percentage by hand. The compact housing fits where the larger 600 will not.

The manual control is the catch. You must lower the humidity setting as the weather gets colder, or windows will fog and moisture will condense inside the walls. Compared with the 600 at 17 gallons and automatic control, it is less capable and more demanding. Compared with the 300, it needs the furnace blower and a bypass duct, while the 300 is self-contained.

It installs on a supply or return plenum with a water line and a drain, and it needs only low-voltage wiring. Maintenance is a yearly water panel change and a quick drain check. For a modest home with a suitable furnace, a manual setpoint is manageable, but have the installer show you how to adjust it by outdoor temperature. A licensed HVAC professional should handle the cut-in and plumbing.
products.bestFor: Smaller homes with a suitable furnace that need modest humidification at a low cost.

products.name: AprilAire 800 Automatic Steam Humidifier

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: 11.5 to 34.6 gallons per day, 6 output levels

specList.label: Coverage
specList.value: Up to 10,300 sq ft in tightly built homes

products.description:
The 800 is a different machine. Instead of evaporating water from a panel using furnace air, it heats water with electrodes and injects steam into the duct. AprilAire gives six output levels from 11.5 to 34.6 gallons per day depending on voltage and installation, and rates it for up to 10,300 square feet in a tightly built home. It is for very large houses, homes with high ceilings and leaky envelopes, and spaces such as attics or crawl spaces where evaporative models are impractical.

The cost is energy and installation. Making steam draws a lot of electricity, far more than an evaporative panel, and it needs a dedicated electrical circuit, often 240 volt, installed by an electrician. Compared with the 720AKZ at 21 gallons, it can deliver up to about 65 percent more moisture. Compared with the 700, it does not need the furnace running, since it generates steam on its own.

The electrodes need impurities in the water to conduct, so purified water is not required, and filtering is not recommended. Maintenance means replacing the steam cylinder periodically, and mineral buildup is part of the design. Because of the high electrical load and the need to tie into the ducts, it should be installed by a licensed HVAC professional and an electrician.
products.bestFor: Very large or leaky homes that need up to 34 gallons per day and have the electrical capacity.

Works without relying on furnace airflow
Does not need filtered or purified water
Six output levels adapt to voltage and installation
cons: Steam generation draws much more electricity than evaporative
Needs a dedicated circuit installed by an electrician
Steam cylinder is a periodic replacement part

buyingCriteria.criterion: Gallons per day versus house size
buyingCriteria.explanation: Rated capacity is the water a unit can evaporate in a day, and the square foot coverage assumes a tightly built home. The 500M rates 12 gallons for 3,600 square feet, the 300 13 gallons for 3,900, the 600 and 400 17 gallons for 5,000, the 700 18 gallons for 5,300, the 720AKZ 21 gallons for 6,250 and the 800 up to 34.6 gallons for 10,300. A leaky or older house needs a model rated for more area than its actual size, so step up one tier.

Bypass models such as the 400, 500M and 600 use the furnace blower and a pressure difference between supply and return ducts to push air through the panel, so output depends on the furnace running. Fan-powered models such as the 700, 720AKZ and 300 have their own fan and work independently of duct pressure. Steam models such as the 800 boil water and need no airflow from the furnace. Pick the type that matches your system and how often it runs.

Furnace-mounted units attach to the warm-air plenum of a forced-air furnace or heat pump. The 300 is the exception, with a self-contained design that AprilAire says works with boilers, mini-splits, radiant heat and ductless systems. Check your system type and the plenum space before you choose. A heat pump with low supply temperatures may reduce evaporative output because cooler air carries less moisture.

Humidity setpoints must fall as outdoor temperatures drop, or moisture condenses on windows and inside walls. The 700, 720AKZ, 600, 400 and 800 are automatic and adjust to outdoor temperature using a second sensor. The 500M and 300 are manual, so you change the setting by hand as the weather changes. A forgotten manual setting is the main cause of foggy windows.

Draining units such as the 600 flush minerals away, while the drainless 400 evaporates all the water, so scale stays on the panel. The 720AKZ cuts wastewater by 60 percent versus the 700 using a recirculation valve. All evaporative models need a new water panel each heating season, and hard water shortens its life. Know your water hardness before you choose.

These humidifiers cut into the duct plenum, tap a water line, run a drain and connect to a control, and fan-powered and steam units need line-voltage wiring. A bad water line over a furnace can cause damage, and wrong ducting reduces output. Have a licensed HVAC professional install the unit, and a licensed electrician for the 800's dedicated circuit.

howWeEvaluated.description: We sorted models by bypass, fan-powered and steam design, since that decides whether output depends on the furnace. The 700, 720AKZ and 300 were treated as independent of duct pressure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and automation
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared automatic dual-sensor control on the 700, 720AKZ, 600, 400 and 800 with the manual humidistats of the 500M and 300. Manual units were rated lower for convenience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Water and maintenance
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared drain behavior, such as the 400's drainless operation and the 720AKZ's 60 percent wastewater cut, and the annual panel change on each. Hard water was treated as a major factor.

howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the work each model demands, from low-voltage wiring on the bypass units to 120 V on fan units and a dedicated circuit on the 800, plus the 720AKZ's 5 year warranty.

maintenance.why: The panel collects mineral scale and loses efficiency. A clogged panel cuts output and can cause odors.

maintenance.task: Clean the distribution tray and water feed
maintenance.why: Scale blocks the small water holes. A vinegar soak removes it, and clean parts keep the water evenly spread.

maintenance.task: Check the drain line and saddle valve
maintenance.why: A clogged drain can overflow onto the furnace. Check that water drains freely.

maintenance.interval: At the end of the heating season
maintenance.why: Standing water grows bacteria and mold. Turn off the water and set the control to off.
Calibration drifts. A cheap hygrometer cross-checks the control.

maintenance.why: Mineral buildup eventually fouls the electrodes. Follow the maker's service steps.

faq.q: Should I install an AprilAire humidifier myself?
faq.a: Have a licensed HVAC professional install it. The job involves cutting the duct plenum, tapping a water line, running a drain, wiring a control and, for the fan-powered and steam models, line-voltage power. Mistakes can leak water onto the furnace or wire the unit wrongly. The 800 steam unit also needs a dedicated circuit from an electrician.

faq.q: What is the difference between the 400 and the 600?
faq.a: Both are bypass models rated for 17 gallons per day and about 5,000 square feet. The 400 evaporates all the water that flows to the panel and does not need a continuous drain, while the 600 drains water through the panel and flushes minerals away. The 400 saves water but scales faster in hard water.

faq.q: Does a fan-powered humidifier work better than a bypass?
faq.a: It works more consistently. A bypass unit depends on the furnace blower and duct pressure, so output varies. The 700, 720AKZ and 300 have their own fans, so they do not depend on the furnace being on. The tradeoff is a 120 volt connection and a higher price.

faq.q: What humidity level should I set?
faq.a: AprilAire says 40 to 60 percent is the healthy range, but in cold weather that is too high for many houses and causes condensation on windows. Automatic models lower the setpoint as the outdoor temperature drops. For manual models like the 500M and 300, lower it by hand to roughly 30 to 35 percent when it is very cold outside.

faq.q: How often does the water panel need changing?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season, and more often in hard water. The panel traps minerals, and a clogged panel reduces output and can smell. The 720AKZ uses a one-piece HydroCore cartridge that makes the change simpler.

faq.q: Can I use an AprilAire with a heat pump or boiler?
faq.a: Fan-powered models such as the 700 and 720AKZ attach to forced-air furnaces and heat pumps. For boilers, radiant heat and mini-splits, AprilAire says the 300 can be used. Heat pumps deliver cooler air than furnaces, which lowers evaporative output, so an installer should size the unit up.
